# Incident Report — MTA 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** |
| Windows domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (Kerberos realm BEPOSITIVE) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS CNameString exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller at 172.17.0.17) |

The gateway/DC on this LAN segment is 172.17.0.17 (also seen answering DNS on UDP/53 and SMB/Kerberos on 445/139/88).

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not behavioral. The provided Suricata/ET alert export flags 48 events as:

```
ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2
172.17.0.99 -> 79.124.78.197  (sport=49813 -> dport=80)
```

This is corroborated by direct inspection of the reassembled HTTP streams: the host repeatedly POSTs to `/foots.php` on 79.124.78.197 with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, and a body matching the pattern `<code>|<GUID>|<payload>`, e.g.:

```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
```

Bot/victim GUID observed: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`. First check-in occurs at ~T+155s into the capture (2024-09-04 17:35 UTC) and repeats roughly every 60–90 seconds through the end of the capture (~1hr), consistent with a stealer/loader heartbeat rather than a one-time infection event. No executable/PE payload transfer is present in this capture (all `foots.php`/`index.php` responses are short chunked acks of a few bytes) — the initial binary drop happened outside the capture window.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — primary Koi Stealer C2 (raw IP used as HTTP Host header, no domain — matches ET rule "GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser")
- User-Agent used for all C2 traffic: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (C2 checkin, repeated ~50 times)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (gate/affiliate-tracking GET, returns `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST, 105-byte encrypted body)

**Malicious/notable domains:** none — the C2 uses a bare dotted-quad IP, no DNS resolution was performed for it. No domain in the DNS query list correlates to the C2 IP.

**Transferred files / hashes:** none observed. No PE, script, or document object was transferred over HTTP in this capture (verified via `tshark --export-objects http` — all captured objects are small text/ack bodies, none begin with an `MZ` header). No SHA256 can be computed from this evidence; the dropper/initial-access vector is not present in the capture window.

**Excluded as non-indicators (checked and ruled out):**
- TLS session to `46.254.34.201` (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — encrypted, not referenced in the Suricata alerts, no corroborating evidence of maliciousness.
- HTTP GET to `acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` — legitimate Adobe ARM update-ping telemetry (response body is literally `****`), not part of the alert set.
- GPL SMB/Kerberos "overflow"/"DOS attempt" alerts between 172.17.0.99 and the DC (172.17.0.17) on ports 139/445/88 — reviewed the raw traffic; this is routine domain-joined authentication/SMB traffic (old generic GPL signatures are known to false-positive on benign NTLMSSP/Kerberos negotiation). No exploit payload or lateral-movement artifact was found.

## Summary

DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on BEPOSITIVE.COM, is infected with **Koi Stealer**, beaconing to C2 **79.124.78.197:80** via `/foots.php` and `/index.php` starting at 2024-09-04 17:35 UTC and continuing for the full ~1-hour capture. Attribution rests on the ETPRO signature match plus manually-verified HTTP stream content matching the known Koi Stealer POST format. No malware binary or exfiltrated file was captured in this PCAP; only the ongoing C2 checkin traffic is present.
